## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyabāhuppacālaka-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 18) is a training rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic bodily decorum, specifically concerning the practice of swinging the arms while sitting in inhabited areas [SuttaCentral]. In modern grammatical analysis of the Pātimokkha, Steven Collins notes that Sekhiya 18 forms part of a sequence of rules (Sekhiya 18–28) containing adverbial or "quasi-gerund" constructions ending in *-akaṃ* [Collins 1993]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali under the title *Swinging the arms* [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate extensive cross-sectarian transmission of this training rule across Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. Parallels exist in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and both Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, as well as the Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Corresponding rules are preserved in Sanskrit fragments and Chinese translations of the Dharmaguptaka (e.g., Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 17), Mahīśāsaka (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 34), and Sarvāstivāda traditions (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 44), as well as Mūlasarvāstivāda Pātimokkha texts [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 106 text-reuse matches across 41 texts, reflecting the highly patterned, formulaic phrasing shared between Sekhiya 18 and adjacent Sekhiya rules, especially Sekhiyas 11, 15, 12, 6, 48, 44, and 24 [DharmaNexus].
